text:
alex: heads-up — seeing sustained queue growth on GPU pool eu-west-1 since 08:46 UTC, queued requests ~3.2k, p99 latency spiking and hosted API 502/504s increasing. creating thread to track.
ops-bot: ALERT: gpu_pool_saturation[euw1] threshold=100% queued=3207 errors=450 rate=+1200m/s
maria: thanks alex. are autoscaler logs showing scale attempts?
jin: looking now — autoscaler recorded scale-down embargo until 08:45 due to metric anomaly, then failed to launch new nodes because instance quota returned ENI limit. snippet from scaler logs: ```ERROR: launch failed: InsufficientInstanceCapacity: Unable to satisfy request for 4 x p4d.12xlarge (InsufficientInstanceCapacity)```
noah: wait — we patched the admission-controller config at 06:30 to set per-gpu-concurrency=12 (was 16) to try to reduce OOMs. could that reduce throughput and push more requests into queue? :thinking_face:
samira: yes — lower concurrency + quota shortage = fewer active sessions -> queue backlog. also fallback routing started sending traffic to us-east-1 and ap-southeast-1. those pools started nearing capacity too.
alex: timeline so far: 06:30 config change (per-gpu-concurrency=12), 08:10 sudden traffic jump from enterprise customer X (~2.5x), 08:20 regional autoscaler embargo due to anomaly, 08:46 queue >3k and API errors.
maria: can we verify fallback routing events? jin can you paste the routing decisions?
jin: from routing logs: ```2026-03-18T08:41:22Z route_decision: fallback eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 reason=queue_depth>threshold count=1800``` another: ```08:44 fallback us-east-1 -> ap-southeast-1 reason=latency_spike count=600```
noah: so a small config change reduced throughput margin, autoscaler couldn't get capacity because of cloud quota/spot shortages, routing cascaded and amplified load. classic feedback loop.
samira: mitigation applied at 08:50: increased per-gpu-concurrency back to 16 (hotfix), scaled up dedicated pool in eu-west-1 + emergency quota request for cores, and temporarily disabled cross-region fallback for affected customers.
alex: what immediate effect? metrics?
jin: p95/p99 dropped within ~90s after hotfix. queue dropped from 3207 -> 400 by 08:58. hosted API errors back to baseline by 09:02.
maria: good. root causes: 1) risky change to admission controller concurrency without capacity test, 2) autoscaler embargos masking needed scale-up, 3) cloud quota/spot capacity shortage. any other contributors?
noah: small thing — our preflight for admission changes didn't include load replay test against realistic traffic shape. that would've shown the throughput regression.
samira: also we don't have a precheck that cross-region fallback will obey per-customer routing caps; that allowed customers to be bounced around and contribute to hotspots elsewhere.
alex: agreed. let's list action items (short):
- rollback-safe deploy: require staged canary + load-replay for admission-controller config changes (owner: eng-runtime)
- autoscaler: add improved error handling for quota/launch failures and a fallback to controlled capacity-bump (owner: eng-infra)
- quota playbook: automate emergency quota request + pre-provision buffer for critical regions (owner: eng-ops)
- routing: add per-customer fallback caps and circuit-breaker to avoid cross-region storming (owner: eng-platform)
- post-incident: run a tabletop sim for failure mode where concurrency drops + quota shortage (owner: SRE)
- observability: add a composite alert that combines queue depth + launch-fail rate so we don't get blind autoscaler embargos (owner: devex)
